Heavy social burden: 3 English listeners must label 40-60 natural attempts per measure in weeks 3-6, 2-3 French listeners check noisy clips, and panel rounds run 2-3 times a cycle with 10% repeat clips. Many solo learners cannot sustain this.

Scoring means uploading a WAV to the server, with no streaming during speech. The latency budget is 0.8 + ~0.2 + 1-3 s, with no evidence behind it. Speaking feedback needs the network, and offline takes wait in an outbox. Commute practice suffers.
Hosting option H1 (home server + tunnel) means 'scoring works only while the home machine is on'. From the learner's side, the speaking half of sessions would fail unpredictably.

The 8-week cycle packs stress, three vowel sets, /h/, fluency and sentence stress. GOOSE-FOOT gets 1 week of listening then speaking, and TRAP-STRUT-LOT 1 week of each. The default 10-minute session juggles 3 targets across 6 blocks. That is fragmented and gives each contrast less than the ~8 sessions the addendum suggests.
Free speech in the default 10-minute session is a single 55-s 'Use it' answer. The retell appears only in 15-minute sessions.
Most of its value (Measurement Lab, registry, trust promotion) goes to the developer, not the learner.
fatal_flaws: Every speaking verdict (vowels, /h/, stress) is gated behind reaching 'Trusted': known-answer AUC ≥ .85 AND κ ≥ .60 against a 3-listener majority on ≥40 natural attempts per measure. The design itself rates 'No human listeners available' as a Medium-likelihood, High-impact risk. If listeners cannot be recruited or cannot agree, the learner never gets corrective speaking feedback, which is the mechanism Add. §5.4 and Brief §2 #5 rate most important for speaking. The app then stays a listening trainer with bars that give no verdict.

Conditional: if hosting option H1 is chosen, speaking practice works only while a home computer is on and reachable, which is incompatible with short phone sessions whenever and wherever the learner has time.
wrong_or_unverified_claims: Its reason for server-side scoring ('spoken-phoneme output needs the SDK') does not require a server. The browser JS SDK also exposes nbestPhonemeCount, phonemeAlphabet and enableProsodyAssessment, as evidence-max and learner-ux confirmed in the SDK source and types. Server scoring is a choice, not a necessity.

The latency budget (upload about 0.2 s; Azure plus Parselmouth 1-3 s; total ≤3 s) is unverified. Reported Azure pronunciation-assessment tail latency reaches about 20 s for about 5% of requests (Azure-Samples issue #1327, older SDK).
Internal inconsistency: 'Vowel pairs get about 8 sessions each' does not fit the week plan, which gives GOOSE-FOOT and TRAP-STRUT-LOT about 1-2 weeks at 3 English sessions a week.
'Apple developer account ($99 a year, unverified)': the other designs verified it on Apple's membership page.
'Safari 26 records stereo when echo cancellation is off' rests on one third-party blog.
Hetzner prices after the June 2026 increase come from secondary blogs.
best_ideas_to_graft: 'Couldn't judge this one clearly — no verdict': ambiguous results are shown neutrally and excluded from statistics, never shown as errors.
A measurement registry with trust levels and promotion rules, run by the developer outside learner sessions, never as in-session calibration chores.
Known-answer checks on TTS right and wrong versions and native recordings (V4: ≥95% on native speech, or the measure is broken). Cheap and needs no learner time.
'Try again — without the model' as the self-correction button label.
Show dose as attempts per target ('18 attempts on FLEECE–KIT this week').
A rule to shorten the default session and move the reminder after 3 weeks below 3 sessions a week.

key_decision_axes: Time to first real practice versus completeness: a slice with offline listening in about 2-3 weeks (lean-mvp) or a Stress Starter in about 5-8 weeks (learner-ux), versus a full program before practice starts (evidence-max about 8-12 weeks; measurement's validated speaking feedback about 9-10 weeks).

What the learner gets from an unvalidated scorer: nothing or bars with no verdict (measurement, and lean-mvp and evidence-max for stress), versus a graded trust ladder with self-check plus model and confident-only hints (learner-ux). This decides whether the speaking half feels useful in the first weeks.

Who carries the validation work: developer-side batches and TTS/native known-answer sets, versus deliberate-error recording inside the learner's sessions and recurring human listener panels as a gate on feedback.

How much free speech is in the default session: Use/Retell in every session including 5 minutes (learner-ux, lean-mvp in Standard), versus a short 'use it' task with retell only in 15-minute sessions (evidence-max, measurement). This drives transfer to conversation.

Where scoring runs and how it reaches the learner: the browser Azure SDK streaming with a 10-minute token (lower latency, no server to keep awake) versus WAV upload to a Python server (needs the network, adds a hop, the home-server option can be down).

When the native-French clarity track arrives and how engaging it is: in the MVP as a 5-minute extension (learner-ux) or deferred (lean-mvp E8, evidence-max F9, measurement E11). Also paired-takes-only versus an ASR listener game in noise.

Cycle length and per-contrast dose: an 8-week first cycle (faster first report) versus 12 weeks (closer to the stress-hours target). One contrast at a time versus two or three at once. Four-week blocks per sound (risk of boredom) versus about 8 sessions per pair.
What counts toward the weekly goal: listening-only sessions, 3-minute sessions, exits after 3 minutes. Too loose dilutes the dose; too strict makes missed weeks more likely.
Burden of progress measurement: Check length and frequency, repeatability re-recordings, panel logistics (exported zip plus CSV, or an in-app listener link).

red_team_issues.problem: Section 2.8 says the CI key scan fails the build if the bundle contains the header name `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`. The Azure Speech SDK itself contains that string. I checked the npm package: SDK 1.51.0's minified browser bundle has `HeaderNames.AuthKey = "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key"`, so every build that bundles the SDK would fail. The likely result is that someone switches the key check off.
red_team_issues.fix: Scan every bundle file for the real key value and the name `AZURE_SPEECH_KEY`. Scan only the app's own code, not the SDK chunk, for the header name and for calls to `SpeechConfig.fromSubscription`. The reason and the check are now in section 2.8 and Appendix A.

red_team_issues.problem: Word stress (rank 1) is overclaimed and the numbers contradict each other. The 10-minute session timeline gives stress about 2 min 10 s (1:10 listening, 1:00 speaking). That is about 10 minutes a week and about 2 hours over 12 weeks, not the 20 minutes a week and 4 hours that the dose table claims. The table says the plan 'matches the addendum's estimate of about 4 hours', which is false. Option A's risk line ('about 2 hours by week 8') is also wrong: it is about 1.3 hours.
red_team_issues.fix: Restated the stress dose as about 2 hours, about half the addendum's estimate, in 2.3, EN-1, the 6.3 dose table and note, Option A's risks and the evidence map. Added a choice to D8: about 2 minutes of stress per session (the default) or about 4 minutes, which reaches about 4 hours but halves the sound-block time.

red_team_issues.problem: Option B's French timing does not add up. The 12-week program table starts French in practice weeks 1–4, but slice 4 (French) ships at build weeks ~10–12. Practice starts at build weeks 3–5, so French actually starts around practice week 6–10. Cycle 1 then gives only about 5–10 French sessions. Reason #1 of the recommendation ('serves both of your goals in cycle 1') overstates this. S7 ('from week 6') and the week-4 rate check cannot be reached on that timeline.
red_team_issues.fix: Corrected the French column of the program table, the timelines, reason #1, Option B's risks and the comparison table. The week-8 French Check now doubles as a second baseline when French has not started. Added decision D14, which offers an early French first version: it needs only the audio core and moves slices 2–3 about a week later.

red_team_issues.problem: The listener-panel size misreads the brief. Brief §3.7 and §7 cap. 1 call for 3–5 *trained* listeners or about 10 untrained ones. The document says '3–5 instructed', and D6 recommends 3–5 friends. Friends are untrained listeners, so 3–5 of them is below the evidence.
red_team_issues.fix: Changed the wording to '3–5 trained or about 10 untrained; friends with a short briefing count as untrained' in 2.2, 6.7, D6 and the evidence map.

red_team_issues.problem: The noisy café (FR-4) cites noise-while-speaking evidence (Add. §3.3 #4; Garnier 2018), but the design mixes noise into the recording afterwards. You never hear noise while you speak. Playing noise in earbuds while recording would break the audio rules, and Bluetooth headset mics degrade the audio. The only evidence that applies is the partner who sometimes mishears (Buz 2016).
red_team_issues.fix: FR-4 and the evidence map now say that noise is mixed in after recording, that the mishearing-partner mechanism is the evidence, and that noise heard while speaking is not used. The 20–30% mishearing target is labelled a working rule.

red_team_issues.problem: S7 overclaims. It expects the clear-minus-usual gain at your usual speed (±10%) to 'pass' with Moderate evidence, but keeping clarity at normal speed is Weak (Add. §3.3 #3), and only about 23 of 41 talkers gave a significant benefit (Add. §3.2). Also, 'stays above zero' can be met at baseline, so it does not test training.
red_team_issues.fix: Rewrote S7 as the week-12 gain beating the week-0 gain by more than the day-to-day spread. The expectation is now 'uncertain', with the Weak and None found labels. Added the 23-of-41 caveat to 2.4.

red_team_issues.problem: The roadmap claims 'If you stop after R6, plus a small part of R10, you have Option A'. But Option A includes the /h/ block, which is in R7. Section 5 also claims 'the first three slices of A and B are the same', but B's slice 3 comes later because R5 (backup) comes first.
red_team_issues.fix: Changed to 'R1–R6, the /h/ part of R7 and the core of R10'. The first two slices are the same, and B's third comes about a week later.

red_team_issues.problem: Build estimates are optimistic and do not match each other. Slice 1 at build weeks 3–5 needs R1+R2+R3, which is 12–40 developer-days at the stated epic sizes. B's epics add up to about 11–28 weeks, against the claimed 16–20. Option A's 8–11 weeks is below B's own sizing for the same work. 'Build week' is never defined (full-time or part-time).
red_team_issues.fix: Defined build weeks as full-time weeks. Kept R3's pack v0 small so R3 is size M. Restated slice 1 as ~3–6, B as ~16–22 (epic sums ~11–26), A as ~9–12 (40–60 developer-days), and adjusted all timelines to match.

red_team_issues.problem: Prosody is 'stored only' (6.10), yet D2 says to move to the paid S0 tier 'if F0 lacks prosody'. That means paying for a feature nothing uses. Section 2.7 also says prosody is 'turned on only where it is used', which does not fit 'stored only'.
red_team_issues.fix: Prosody is now requested only on Check retells and anchors and stored for comparison. D2 moves to S0 only on reaching the audio limit. Whether F0 includes prosody is marked as not affecting the decision.

red_team_issues.problem: The Azure audio budget was never estimated. The recommended free-speech path (transcript first, then scripted assessment) sends each retell twice. Build-time TTS contrast checks, the validation sittings and re-scoring can add 2–4 audio hours in some months, so F0's 5 hours can run out. F0's single request slot (checked: not adjustable) is also shared between laptop tools and the phone.
red_team_issues.fix: Added an audio budget to 2.7: about 6 minutes of audio per 10-minute session and about 2.5 hours a month in practice. Laptop tools run on a separate S0 resource or are spread over months. Updated the S0 cost ranges ($3–8 for B), the usage warning and the risks.

red_team_issues.problem: Held-out items cannot cover 5 Checks. There are 5 Checks (weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, 16) but only 4 stress forms, and each form has 30 words while a Check uses 20. The /uː–ʊ/ set holds out only 8 pairs (16 words), but Checks need 10 words per contrast each time, 50 in total. /æ–ʌ–ɑ/ and /h/ are also short.
red_team_issues.fix: Added 5 forms (A = baseline to E = week 16). Stress held-out is now 150 items (20 for speaking, 10 for listening, per form). Speaking probes use any word containing the sound (50 per target). Listening pairs may repeat across Checks in new test voices.

red_team_issues.problem: Section 6.3 lets the baseline alone skip a block ('already fine'). Brief §7 cap. 2 says onboarding findings are only candidates. The document's own evidence gate needs 15–20 instances, from 5 words, over 3 sessions.
red_team_issues.fix: A block is now skipped only after probe slots meet the evidence gate, with the upper end of the error range below 0.20.

red_team_issues.problem: Clusters are 'monitored only', and Brief §5.1 is cited as support. In fact Brief §5.1 ranks keeping consonants in initial and medial clusters first for international listeners [Moderate; correlational]. The addendum's last-place rank covers only word-final clusters and is [Not searched].
red_team_issues.fix: Section 2.3 and the evidence map now state the conflict and call it a judgement call. Check probes cover initial, medial and final clusters with 50 held-out words, and the data decide.

red_team_issues.problem: 'It covers every ranked capability in Brief §7 that fits a phone' is an overclaim. The design leaves out the chunk phrase bank (cap. 8), covers cap. 9 only through retells, and covers cap. 12 only in part.
red_team_issues.fix: Rewrote the evidence-fit statement to list which capabilities are covered and which are not.

red_team_issues.problem: The backup design ignores platform limits. Weekly snapshots that include 150–250 MB of rolling practice audio exceed the Worker's 100 MB request-body limit on the free plan (checked). Section 6.11 also offers KV for rate counters, but free KV allows only 1,000 writes a day and is slow to update across locations (checked).
red_team_issues.fix: Backups now hold data plus baseline, Check and anchor audio only, uploaded in encrypted parts under 100 MB (API and roadmap updated). Tokens and counters go in D1, not KV. Also noted that R2 asks for a payment method (secondary).

red_team_issues.problem: The first-attempt rule contradicts itself. 'Only first attempts count' conflicts with 'a correct retry … counts as a self-correction' and with the evidence map's 'self-corrections weigh more'.
red_team_issues.fix: Self-corrections are now logged as a separate sign of progress and never enter the error estimate. Labelled as a design inference from Brief §3.2.

red_team_issues.problem: Two sections handle 'no verdict' results differently. Section 2.6 #10 says the audio is 'scored later, for statistics only'. Section 6.5 and the target model say it is left out of statistics.
red_team_issues.fix: Both now say the audio may be scored later for validation but never enters the target model or any statistic.

red_team_issues.problem: Several evidence claims are stronger than the brief. 'Nobody has published test–retest data' (the brief says none was *found*). 'No study shows…' (the brief says no *controlled* study was found). The De Fino finding is widened from L2 French to all L2 speech. 'The evidence requires everything'.
